summary: Consumer innovation money is flowing to AI glasses and health wearables: Meta and EssilorLuxottica sold over 7 million glasses in 2025, and sales nearly doubled again in Q2 2026. Oura postponed its planned $2.2 billion IPO on September 29, 2026, citing market uncertainty, so the ring leader stays private for now. Cash pay health (GLP-1s through telehealth and direct from the drug maker) is the largest new consumer spend line, and AI shopping traffic is growing fast. Checkout inside AI agents is now live at Meta Muse through Shopify, but there is no volume data yet.

innovations.name: AI glasses and personal AI devices
innovations.what: Glasses, rings and small screenless gadgets with cameras, microphones and an AI assistant built in. They aim to take some jobs away from the phone.
innovations.stage_why: Meta glasses sold over 7 million units in 2025 and sales nearly doubled again in Q2 2026, but AI glasses are still about 2 million units a quarter against more than 140 million wearables in total.

evidence.money: Meta and EssilorLuxottica planned 10 million units a year of capacity by end of 2026 and have discussed 20 million. OpenAI bought Jony Ive's io; reports say its first device will not ship before late February 2027 and may be a smart speaker, though a 2026 reveal is still possible. Apple glasses are reported for 2027 (unverified).
evidence.revenue: IDC: 2.25 million AI glasses shipped in Q1 2026, up 167%, with Meta at about 69% share. Oura revenue was $1.21 billion for the nine months to June 30, 2026, up 74%, with 5 million paying members. Its IPO (50 million shares at $40 to $44) was postponed on September 29, 2026.

spreads_to.use: Rings and watches feed sleep, heart and glucose data into care and insurance programs.
Prescription smart glasses sold through optical stores (Ray-Ban, Oakley, Warby Parker).
Low-power AI chips, micro displays and waveguides become a new volume market.

innovations.bottleneck: Optics and chips: display waveguides (Lumus designs, Schott makes them for Meta's display glasses) and low-power AI chips (Qualcomm AR1). EssilorLuxottica controls frames and optical retail.

next_milestone.event: OpenAI device reveal (shipping not before late February 2027); Oura sets a new IPO date
next_milestone.timing: Late 2026 to early 2027; no new Oura date announced as of October 8, 2026

innovations.thesis_broken_if: AI glasses shipment growth falls below 30% a year in 2027 or return rates rise sharply as novelty fades.

innovations.name: At-home diagnostics and continuous health sensors
innovations.what: Tests and sensors people buy without a doctor visit: over the counter glucose sensors, home cancer screening kits, STI tests and mail-in blood panels.
innovations.stage_why: The FDA has cleared over the counter glucose sensors and the first home cervical and STI tests, and blood-test startups are scaling. Most users still pay cash, and insurance coverage is thin.

evidence.cost: OTC glucose sensors were modeled at about $100 a month for Dexcom Stelo and $80 for Abbott Lingo (2024 estimates).
evidence.approvals: FDA authorized the Teal Wand home cervical cancer self-collection device (May 2025) and Visby's first OTC home STI test (March 2025). The FDA's Reagan-Udall Foundation held a meeting on next-generation OTC diagnostics (March 2026).
evidence.money: Teal Health raised a $22 million Series A (September 2026). Hims and Hers bought an at-home lab (Trybe Labs). Function Health bought Getlabs for home blood draws.
evidence.revenue: Dexcom Q2 2026 revenue $1.308 billion, up 13%, with 2026 guide $5.18 to $5.25 billion. Abbott CGM sales above $2 billion in Q2 2026, up 9.5%.

spreads_to.use: Earlier diagnosis and remote monitoring for diabetes, heart and cancer screening.
Glucose data drives personalized diet apps and GLP-1 companion programs.
Employers and plans use home kits to close screening gaps cheaply.

innovations.bottleneck: FDA over the counter clearance plus sensor manufacturing scale. Abbott and Dexcom make most glucose sensors, and lab networks (Quest, Labcorp) process most home samples.

next_milestone.event: Dexcom and Abbott Q3 results (Stelo and Lingo trends); more OTC test clearances
next_milestone.timing: Late October 2026; Dexcom date not yet announced as of October 8, 2026 (last year it reported October 30)

innovations.thesis_broken_if: OTC sensor and home test sales stay a small share of Dexcom and Abbott revenue through 2027 and cash pay users churn.

innovations.name: OTC hearing and vision tech
innovations.what: Hearing help sold without a prescription, including AirPods with a hearing aid mode, and new ways to slow nearsightedness in children with special lenses and eye drops.
innovations.stage_why: OTC hearing aids have been legal since 2022 and AirPods can act as hearing aids, yet prescription makers keep growing. Myopia control lenses are approved and growing fast, while the first US myopia drug faces an FDA panel October 30, 2026.

evidence.cost: AirPods Pro with hearing aid mode sell for about $250, versus thousands of dollars for prescription pairs.
evidence.approvals: FDA authorized hearing aid software for AirPods Pro (2024). FDA approved the first myopia control spectacle lens (EssilorLuxottica Stellest). FDA advisory committee for Sydnexis SYD-101 low dose atropine confirmed for October 30, 2026, after a 2025 complete response letter and a formal dispute; the drug is already approved in the EU and UK as Ryjunea (licensed to Santen).
evidence.money: Sonova announced on March 23, 2026 it will sell its consumer hearing unit to focus on prescription aids, a sign the money is not in low-end OTC.
evidence.revenue: Demant H1 2026 hearing aid organic growth 9% and raised 2026 EBIT guide to DKK 4.4 to 4.8 billion. Cooper's MiSight myopia lens grew 23% in fiscal Q2 2026.

spreads_to.use: Earbuds and glasses gain medical features, which raises their price and stickiness.
Pharmacies and warehouse clubs sell hearing devices off the shelf.
Earlier hearing treatment may reduce dementia and fall risk in older adults.

innovations.bottleneck: Tiny receivers and hearing chips (Knowles and in-house chips at the big five makers) and the audiologist and optometrist fitting network that the prescription makers and EssilorLuxottica control.

next_milestone.event: FDA advisory committee on SYD-101 atropine for childhood myopia

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Prescription hearing makers keep growing near 9% while OTC unit sales stay small, which would show OTC is not changing the market.

innovations.name: Cash pay GLP-1 and protein-first nutrition
innovations.what: Consumers buying weight loss drugs directly online or from the drug maker, and food companies reshaping products for smaller, higher protein meals. This replaces the original 'personalized nutrition' item, because this is where consumer money is actually moving.
innovations.stage_why: Direct cash pay channels now reach millions (Hims has 2.9 million subscribers, and one in three new branded weight loss patients in 2025 started on Lilly's self-pay vials). Food makers are relabeling, but packaged-food sales gains are still small.

evidence.cost: Foundayo self pay starts at $149 a month. Whey protein concentrate rose from $1.52 a pound in January 2026 to as high as $2.18 in July 2026 as protein demand outran supply.
evidence.approvals: TrumpRx.gov launched February 2026 with cash prices for GLP-1s and other drugs.
evidence.money: LillyDirect partnered with Walmart pharmacy for pickup at direct-to-consumer prices. Conagra put 'GLP-1 friendly' labels on 26 Healthy Choice meals; Nestle launched Vital Pursuit for GLP-1 users.
evidence.revenue: Hims Q2 2026 revenue about $753 million, up about 38%, with 2,891,000 subscribers; 2026 guide raised to $3.1 to $3.3 billion. BellRing (Premier Protein) June quarter sales $570.4 million, up only 4%. PepsiCo Q3 2026 (Oct 8): organic revenue up 3.1% and it cut its 2026 core EPS growth outlook as the North American turnaround takes longer; Reuters reported GLP-1 use reached 21% of US households in May 2026, up from 9% in January 2025.

spreads_to.use: Drug makers bypass insurers and PBMs by selling direct.
Higher demand and prices for whey and other proteins; pull for fermentation-made proteins.
Pharmacy pickup and in-store GLP-1 sections bring traffic to Walmart and grocers.

innovations.bottleneck: The drug itself: Lilly and Novo set cash prices and choose which telehealth and retail partners can sell branded product. For food, the bottleneck is protein supply (whey) and shelf space.

next_milestone.event: Medicare negotiated semaglutide price takes effect, resetting cash price expectations

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Insurers and Medicare cover most GLP-1 use, so cash pay channels shrink, or Hims subscriber growth turns negative.

innovations.name: AI commerce and shopping agents
innovations.what: Chatbots and AI agents that find, compare and eventually buy products for the shopper. Payment networks are building ways for an agent to pay safely on the user's behalf.
innovations.stage_why: AI-referred shopping traffic is growing fast and converts better than other traffic. Checkout inside agents is live again (Meta Muse with Shop Pay since September 2026), but no purchase volume has been disclosed, so it stays a pilot.

evidence.money: Visa launched Intelligent Commerce Connect (April 8, 2026); Mastercard has Agent Pay. Shopify connected eligible US stores to ChatGPT on March 24, 2026. OpenAI built its checkout protocol with Stripe. On September 21, 2026 Shopify brought Shop Pay checkout to Meta's Muse agent across its merchants; Amazon blocks Muse from buying on its site.
evidence.revenue: eMarketer projects about $20.6 billion of US retail spend through AI agents in 2026, nearly 4 times 2025. Adobe: AI traffic to US retail sites up 393% in Q1 2026, converting 42% better than other traffic by March 2026. Adobe forecasts record US online holiday sales of $275.1 billion (up 6.7%) with AI-referred retail visits up about 130% y/y (forecast released September 2026). Reports say ChatGPT Instant Checkout had about 30 live Shopify merchants in February 2026 and was pulled March 4, 2026, as Walmart saw in-chat checkout convert at a third of its own site (sources conflict on details).

spreads_to.use: Spending shifts from search and retail media ads to being picked by the AI agent.
Tokenized cards and agent identity checks become new network services.
Agents book flights and hotels end to end, pressuring online travel agencies.

innovations.bottleneck: Trusted payment credentials and clean product data. Visa, Mastercard and Stripe control agent payment tokens, Shopify controls many merchants' catalogs, and OpenAI and Google control the shopper's attention.

next_milestone.event: First holiday season with agent checkout live (Muse with Shop Pay); Adobe actuals versus its 130% AI traffic growth forecast

innovations.thesis_broken_if: AI-referred traffic growth falls below 100% a year and agent checkout volume stays negligible through holiday 2026.
